editorial_policy: Independently confirm only the exact Weiser claim supported; do not generalise a modern or different-rite witness.
Same-author Francis X Weiser 1964 reprints are not independent corroboration of Weiser 1958's claims.
Separate secondary historical and geographical context from devotional how-to guidance.
Preserve the unmerged Assumption-herb integration in PR #1512; no parallel new custom.
Preserve the existing 1962 calendar and Mass reader; no action to generate priestly blessings or obligations.
No source text reproduction except factual names, independent editorial paraphrase, short locators.

witnesses.title: Advent straw added to an empty manger for good works

source.issuer: Catholic Culture, independent 2014 essay by Jennifer Gregory Miller

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Contemporary independent Catholic family firsthand practice, explicitly describes a French-origin custom in which children put straw in the manger after prayers and good deeds. French origin is a traditional attribution, not documented in modern France by this source.

witnesses.title: St Stephen feast-day gifts to poor

source.issuer: Catholic Culture, Mary Reed Newland via Homemade Christians

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Catholic family guide instructs using 26 December as a time to read Acts 6–7 and give useful gifts to the poor. No requirement for money, purchase or novel St Stephen rite.

witnesses.title: Ukrainian Christmas Eve kutia

source.issuer: Smithsonian Folklife, Tetiana Poshyvailo

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: First-person Ukrainian cultural account documents wheat-berry, honey and poppy seed dish in Christmas Eve family meal. Pagan divination and dead-spirit beliefs are reported historically only, never recommended.

witnesses.title: Catholic Lenten altar Hunger Cloth

source.issuer: Archdiocese of Munich and Freising — Lenten custom

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Official Catholic source describes Fastentuch before altar in some churches, a Lenten visual penitential custom. Liturgical rubrics and placement are not fixed for all parishes.

witnesses.title: Mothering Sunday visit to a mother church

source.issuer: English Heritage — Mother's Day

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Historic UK fourth Sunday of Lent: people visited their mother churches (places of baptism), and families gathered. Cultural historical claim verified, not a universal Roman Catholic 1962 law.

witnesses.title: Mothering Sunday family visit with simnel cake

source.issuer: Catholic Culture — Bury Simnel Cake, account of historical English custom

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: British family custom associates mother-visiting and simnel cake with fourth Lent Sunday. The claim does not establish obligatory observance and overlaps Mothering Sunday mother-church visit without being identical.
witnesses.owner_handling: Related variant to Mothering Sunday, not separate feast

witnesses.title: Good Friday cross-marked buns in England

source.issuer: English Heritage — Dr Eleanor Barnett, History of Hot Cross Buns

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Documented English Good Friday eating and selling cross-marked spiced buns by eighteenth century. Ancient pagan origin, miraculous healing and protective charm claims remain unverified or rejected.

witnesses.title: Easter Monday Emmaus spiritual walk

source.issuer: Archdiocese of Munich-Freising — Emmausgang

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Catholic archdiocesan explanation specifically documents Bavarian/Austrian Easter Monday family or parish walks tied to Luke 24:13–35, sometimes concluding at church or shrine.

witnesses.title: Lamb as symbol of the risen Christ and paschal sacrifice

source.issuer: Benedict XVI — Easter Sunday homily 12 April 2009

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Christ as the Paschal lamb grounded in 1 Corinthians 5:7, with Jewish Paschal typology. This witnesses theological meaning, not historical sheep-meat blessing or exact decorative family use.

witnesses.title: Polish pisanki and Ukrainian pysanky decorated Easter eggs

source.issuer: Smithsonian Institution — Designing Easter Eggs

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Museum documents named Polish and Ukrainian decorated eggs and Easter exchange, including wax-resist art. Does not validate symbolic lucky charms or mandatory Holy Saturday rites.

witnesses.title: Assumption herb bouquets prepared and blessed locally

source.issuer: Diocese of Augsburg — Maria Himmelfahrt Kräuterweihe

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Official parish describes herbs tied into bouquets by women before the Assumption Mass and blessed locally; future diocese schedules likewise announce herb blessings. Magical healing or lightning protection claims are historical folklore, not Catholic guarantees.
witnesses.owner_handling: PR #1512 overlap / Customs Atlas existing blessing

witnesses.title: Scandinavian St Lucia white-dressed visits and saffron buns

source.issuer: Visit Sweden — Lucia 2025

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Tourism authority documents 13 December white robes, Lucia wreath, saffron buns and light symbolism; predominantly Swedish cultural usage, not specifically a Catholic rite nor true hagiographic account. Prefer LED crown.

witnesses.title: St Stephen horse blessing on 26 December historically

source.issuer: Catholic Culture — The Catholic Cook Book (William Kaufmann ed.)

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Independent Catholic compiled cookbook documents horse blessings in parts of rural Europe, but no named parish, specific 1962 ritual formula or current service is documented.

witnesses.title: Pretzel crossed-arm prayer origin claim

source.issuer: Catholic Culture — Pretzels for God, Francis Weiser (1964)

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Direct derivative of the same author Francis X Weiser rather than an independent witness; ancient Roman crossed-arms, early date, etymology and early manuscript remain unconfirmed.

witnesses.title: Distribution of Lenten pretzels to poor

source.issuer: Catholic Culture — Lent and pretzel

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Same-author folk-custom discussion does not independently prove specifically distributing pretzels to poor in particular historical regions.

witnesses.title: Holy Saturday household dyed eggs and baking

source.issuer: Smithsonian Institution — Easter decorated eggs

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Polish/Ukrainian Easter egg decorating attested, but no explicit household practice specifically on Holy Saturday in cited museum witness.
witnesses.owner_handling: Hold exact date while Easter egg craft remains documented

witnesses.title: French réveillon after Midnight Mass

source.issuer: Roma Capitale tourism — December customs in Rome

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Italian Roman feast and Mass order is documented but does NOT verify French household réveillon specifically after Mass; wrong country and meal timing.

witnesses.title: Ara Coeli Santo Bambino children's prayers

source.issuer: Turismo Roma — Basilica di Santa Maria in Aracoeli

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Rome tourism authority documents longstanding veneration of the Holy Child figure and loss of original sculpture in 1994, but NOT a particular practice of children praying or preaching at Christmas.

witnesses.title: Trinity plague column at Vienna's Graben

source.issuer: Visiting Vienna — Pestsäule

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Vienna's plague column after 1679 and explicit Trinity iconography documented; supports historical landmark context only, not a replicable domestic custom or a general rule for all Trinity shrines.

witnesses.title: Dutch St Nicholas visits imported via diaspora

source.issuer: Catholic Culture — St Stephen and holiday customs

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: A general saints-day household source is not evidence for Dutch migration of Sinterklaas customs. French St Nicholas is verified elsewhere but not the Dutch diaspora transmission claim.

witnesses.title: Christ Child gift bringer and prayer before opening gifts

source.issuer: Archdiocese of Malta — Five family traditions for Advent

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Modern Catholic family gifts and Advent generosity described; specific historical Christkind gift-bringer and household prayer form are not substantiated.

witnesses.title: St Patrick Lorica prayer attribution

source.issuer: Catholic Culture — St Patrick's feast overview

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Common Catholic devotion may be associated with Patrick; without manuscript/provenance evidence, direct authorship or exact received prayer form is unverified.

witnesses.title: Surrexit Dominus vere greeting

source.issuer: Holy See — Easter 2025 Urbi et Orbi

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: Catholic Easter acclamation Christ is risen supported; precise traditional Latin exchange 'Surrexit Dominus vere' and local household greeting date not independently established by this modern address.

witnesses.title: Priestly Easter lamb-meat blessing historical

source.issuer: Archdiocese of Munich-Freising — Easter parish account

witnesses.verified_claim_limit: A 2025 parish newsletter describes Easter lamb cake brought for priestly blessing; that is not corroboration of Weiser's historical blessing of actual lamb meat or a particular 1962 formula.
